35	 *
36	 * 1. **Day page.** One item per calendar day (on the phone's clock) that has at least one entry.
37	 *    Published at the first sync after that day ends. Holds that day's BP readings, glucose readings,
38	 *    dose-log entries and diary notes. The envelope `effective` is the bare date (`2024-10-31`).
39	 *    If the patient later edits or deletes anything on that day, HomeLog publishes a new day page that
40	 *    `supersedes` the old one and restates the whole day.
41	 *
42	 * 2. **My Medicines list.** One item each time the patient saves their medicine list. Holds one
43	 *    `my_med` entry per medicine on the list, including ones marked stopped. Each save restates the
44	 *    whole list and `supersedes` the previous list item. `effective` is the date of the save.
45	 *
46	 * Narrative: on a day page, the narrative is the patient's diary notes for the day, verbatim, one
47	 * paragraph per note. HomeLog adds only the bold time label at the start of each paragraph; the words
48	 * inside the `<ref>` span are exactly what the patient typed (spelling and all). Readings and dose-log
49	 * entries have no narrative. A My Medicines list item has a one-line narrative generated by the app
50	 * ("My Medicines, saved 2 May 2026").
51	 *
52	 * Times: HomeLog stores **wall-clock time as shown on the phone, with no UTC offset and no time-zone
53	 * name** (`"2024-10-31T08:20"`). The app does not know which time zone the phone was in. To place a
54	 * reading on a timeline you need the patient's time zone from somewhere else. Envelope `recorded`
55	 * values are server times in UTC and do carry an offset.
56	 *
57	 * Medicine names are whatever the patient typed or picked; they are not checked against any
58	 * prescription. A self-reported list can differ from every clinic's list, and that is the point of it.
59	 */
60	
61	/** One entry on a HomeLog day page or My Medicines list. */
62	export type HomeLogEntry = BpReading | GlucoseReading | DoseLog | DiaryNote | MyMed;
63	
64	/**
65	 * Local wall-clock date-time as shown on the patient's phone, `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM`, no seconds, no
66	 * offset, no zone. Not UTC. See the module comment.
67	 */
68	type LocalDateTime = string;

70	/** A home blood pressure reading. */

72	  type: 'bp_reading';
73	
74	  /** When the cuff took the reading (cuff clock, synced to the phone), or when the patient says it was taken if typed. Local wall time. */
75	  measured_at: LocalDateTime;
76	
77	  /** Systolic pressure, mmHg. */
78	  systolic_mmhg: number;
79	
80	  /** Diastolic pressure, mmHg. */
81	  diastolic_mmhg: number;
82	
83	  /** Pulse rate from the cuff, beats per minute. Absent when typed in and the patient left it blank. */
84	  pulse_bpm?: number;
85	
86	  /**
87	   * How the reading got into HomeLog.
88	   * - 'cuff_sync': sent by a paired Bluetooth cuff. Values are exactly what the cuff measured.
89	   * - 'typed': typed in by the patient (e.g. cuff not paired, or a reading taken elsewhere such as a
90	   *   pharmacy kiosk). Typos happen; the patient may later fix them, which produces a superseding day page.
91	   * A patient who types in a reading the cuff also synced produces two entries for one measurement;
92	   * HomeLog does not detect this.
93	   */
94	  entry_method: 'cuff_sync' | 'typed';
95	
96	  /** Which arm, if the patient set it in the cuff profile. Absent means not recorded. */
97	  arm?: 'left' | 'right';
98	}

103

105	  measured_at: LocalDateTime;
106	
107	  /**
108	   * The number shown on the meter, in `unit`. HomeLog does **not** convert: the value is in whatever
109	   * unit the meter was set to display at the time.
110	   */

116	   * - 'mmol/L': millimoles per litre (1 mmol/L = 18.016 mg/dL).
117	   * The unit is a meter setting, so it **can change partway through one patient's history** (for

174	   * - 'units': insulin units (UCUM `[iU]`).
175	   * - 'tablets': number of tablets or capsules; the strength is on the My Medicines entry.
176	   * - 'puffs', 'mL': as named.

187	 * `<ref>` span whose id equals this entry's id. The payload holds only the tags the patient picked.
188	 */
189	export interface DiaryNote {
190	  type: 'diary_note';
191	
192	  /** When the patient wrote the note (not necessarily when the symptom started). Local wall time. */
193	  written_at: LocalDateTime;
194	
195	  /**
196	   * Symptom tags the patient picked from HomeLog's list. Empty when the note is not about a symptom.
197	   * The list (fixed in this schema version): 'nausea', 'vomiting', 'diarrhea', 'poor_appetite',
198	   * 'dizzy', 'tired', 'short_of_breath', 'swelling', 'headache', 'cough', 'pain', 'low_mood', 'other'.

232	
233	  /**

241	
242	  /** When the patient started it, from a month picker: `YYYY`, `YYYY-MM` or `YYYY-MM-DD`; precision is the string's precision. Absent if not entered. */

244

257	/**
258	 * Consumer views, version 2: the small shapes a patient-facing chart app reads.
259	 *
260	 * These are defined by the consumer, not by any source. A mapper turns one source's FOLIO record items
261	 * for one patient into these rows. The consumer merges rows from several sources itself, so a mapper
262	 * reports only what its own source says, and never invents, infers from other sources, or "corrects"
263	 * what the source records.

284	 *   used to understand an entry but must not be the only basis for a row.

286	 *   can show the source text behind a fact. Cite at least the item whose entry gives the row's current
287	 *   state.

289	 *   ones it marks restricted, confidential or sensitive. Mark such rows with `sensitivity` (see

`out/transform.ts` is written. It type-checks and runs on the sample patients. I only reviewed the sample output, and the samples have no stopped or held medicines, no retractions and no mmol/L readings. Those paths are untested.

Judgment calls:
- **Scope and corrections:** An item is in scope if its `recorded` time falls on or before `asOf` in America/Chicago. A retracted item's own `supersedes` is ignored, so retracting a bad medicine-list save brings the previous list back. I did this because a retracted save never existed.
- **Medications:** Only the latest current My Medicines list is reported. It gives one row per ingredient, and when an ingredient appears twice the most recent start or stop date wins. All rows are `patient_reported`, and over-the-counter ones set `otc`.
- **Ingredient names:** The ingredient comes from the drug-search display (strength and salt words removed). Otherwise it comes from a brand-to-generic map or a list of known generics. Nicknames like "water pill" get no ingredient, and I never set an RxNorm ingredient code because the picked codes are product-level.
- **Dose:** Tablet counts are turned into milligrams using the strength. A direction with no count, like "morning", means one tablet, and a range like "1 or 2" gives no dose. One sample entry shows the strength mismatch: the patient typed "75 mg" for levothyroxine, but the picked product is 0.075 mg. I used the picked product, so the dose is 75 mcg.
- **Frequency:** Frequency is read from the free-text directions. It is `other` for vague ones like "most days".
- **Status:** A stopped medicine reports its `stopped` date and a reason only when the note clearly gives one. A medicine marked "taking" whose note says "for now", "paused" or similar is `held`. Held rows get no `status_since` because the source gives no date.
- **Sensitivity:** Psychiatric drugs, from a short list I wrote, get `mental-health`.
- **Vitals:**
  - Each home BP and glucose reading is its own row, with times reported as written (no shifting).
  - mmol/L glucose is converted at 18.016 mg/dL per mmol/L and rounded, and HI/LO flags are kept.
  - A typed reading is dropped when a device reading with the same values was taken within 3 minutes.
- **Diary notes and dose logs:** These produce no rows, because the views have nowhere for them.
- **Unreadable input:** Entries the mapper can't read are skipped, and any error returns whatever rows were already built.
